title: On Venus, a Rotation Takes Longer Than a Year
post_title: On Venus, a Rotation Takes Longer Than a Year | QuantaTale
post_description: Imagine a planet where one rotation takes longer than its trip around the Sun. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/ https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Venus_Express/Venus_compared_to_Earth #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Venus has a calendar that sounds impossible. One rotation of Venus relative to the distant stars takes about 243 Earth days. But one orbit around the Sun takes only about 225 Earth days. So its sidereal day is longer than its year. Venus also rotates in the opposite direction to most planets, meaning the Sun would rise in the west. Be careful with the word day: a Venus solar day, from one noon to the next, is about 117 Earth days.
